# Live integration and demo acceptance — October 25, 2026

The authenticated dashboard is live at https://finney-beta.vercel.app. The durable
Finney worker runs OpenCode + Harness2 with app-owned pinned runtimes; isolated
Hermes helpers still provide Gmail access. Runtime code is the merged PR1/PR2
implementation through `b206450`. Personal Hermes settings were not used.

## Actual operating flow

- One labeled synthetic receipt was uploaded through owner-authenticated Storage
  and normal queued intake. OpenCode used five provider calls and Jev reviewed
  its real trace. The agent identified the organizer and USD 153.27 and recorded
  a reported obligation plus a finding. No payment or approval was executed.
- The final review annotation was blocked because a prose classification did not
  match persistence's existing identifier contract. That original blocked result
  and its earlier tool effects remain recorded. The producer/validator alignment
  and missed automatic-diagnosis route were fixed, rather than rewriting output.
- The missed child was recovered once through the ordinary trace-deduplicated
  queue helper, with a separate audit receipt. The original source review was
  not replayed. Diagnosis completed using two reserved calls; its `policy_question`
  output was rejected as `no_source_supported_procedure_defect`. No online search,
  paired evaluation or promotion is claimed from that diagnosis.
- A subsequent read-only director question completed through OpenCode in two
  provider calls and its reply was persisted. It reported the recorded USD 153.27
  liability, unknown cash and no recorded settlement. Its finance tools were
  `get_case`, `read_document`, `get_obligations` and `get_financial_position`.

An actual authenticated browser verified the live case and director reply,
private procedure access, hash-verified baseline/candidate diff and all 56 paired
benchmark result rows. No network interception was used. Unauthenticated finance
access returned 401; authenticated scoped access returned 200.

Final hosted readback retained exactly one reported USD 153.27 obligation with
zero settled amount. Payment, approval and ledger tables were unchanged. The
active skill remained `baseline-v1`; no learned candidate was promoted. Gmail
and Coinbase Wallet connection records were connected, but this acceptance made
no transfer and does not establish settlement readiness. Guest access and other
SSO/account configurations were not part of this authenticated acceptance.

## Learning evidence and limits

The separate [complete benchmark](LEARNING_ACCEPTANCE.md) observed validation
scores of 6/16 for baseline and 11/16 for its candidate. Final heldout scores were
3/12 and 8/12; the candidate was rejected. Startup failures and remaining
stage-blocker errors were retained. Historical outputs were not regraded after
the engineering contract fix, and the final dataset partition stays consumed.

The corpus is source-informed synthetic material, with independent AI review,
not production/customer accuracy evidence. The real captured operating trace
also reconstructed its original case v1, source v1 and pre-action obligations;
later case updates and the subsequently recorded obligation were not backfilled.
Stage/policy interpretation remains an observed weakness, and unknown protected
policy versions remain unassessed rather than gaining authority from a judge.

Release checks passed 797 Python tests and 80 subtests (29 explicit skips), Ruff,
53 web unit tests, TypeScript, production build and 29 browser tests (11 explicit
skips). The final full backend/browser checks ran sequentially. These scripted
checks are separate from the actual provider-backed evidence above.
